newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry wants debate on political system.
newsitem.headline: German industry wants debate on political system.

text.p: Hans-Olaf Henkel, head of the Federation of German Industry (BDI), called on Wednesday for public debate on whether Germany's federal system was flexible enough to respond to modern demands.

Henkel praised a speech by President Roman Herzog given in April criticising politicians for failing to tackle desperately needed reforms while competitor nations looked confidently to the future. A second speech was needed now.

"This should concern itself with the question of whether a country with our federal structure, with 16 federal states and a proportional system of voting, has any chance of adapting as fast as others," Henkel wrote in the weekly Die Woche.
"Somebody must start to talk about the ability of our political system to compete with others," he wrote in the piece released ahead of publication on Thursday.
"Political engineering or constitutional re-engineering has been done in other countries with the justification of increasing adaptability to new circumstances."

Henkel said Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government often had to fight to push forward essential reforms and that nobody could predict if tax reform plans would pass a parliamentary mediation committee due to begin discussing them on Thursday.

Government legislation to introduce 30 billion marks ($17 billion) in income tax cuts over the next two years passed in parliament's lower house but was defeated by the opposition-controlled upper house last week. ($ = 1.759 German Marks)
